title: U.S. Economy Expands at a 3.4% Annual Rate in the Third Quarter
content:
The U.S. economy grew at a 3.4% annualized rate in the third quarter of 2026, accelerating from 2.2% in the second quarter, according to the advance estimate released by the Bureau of Economic Analysis on October 29. The report points to continued momentum in economic activity as the country entered the final quarter of the year.

Growth was supported by increases in investment, consumer spending and government spending. A decline in exports partly offset those gains, while imports increased. The figures are an advance estimate and may be revised as more complete information becomes available.

For businesses, stronger investment and household demand can support sales, but the composition of growth matters. Companies exposed to imported inputs or overseas customers may experience different conditions from firms focused on domestic consumers. Investors will also watch how the data influence expectations for Federal Reserve policy.

The headline growth rate is encouraging, but it does not describe every household or industry. Upcoming revisions, inflation measures and labor-market reports will help show whether the pace is sustainable.

Source: U.S. Bureau of Economic Analysis, October 29, 2026 — https://www.bea.gov/index.php/news/2026/gdp-advance-estimate-3rd-quarter-2026

title: U.S. Consumer Confidence Rebounds in October, but Affordability Concerns Persist
content:
U.S. consumer confidence increased by 7.5 points to 91.7 in October, recovering from September's weaker reading, according to The Conference Board. The improvement reflected better assessments of current business conditions and a stronger short-term outlook among surveyed households.

Easing gasoline prices helped lift sentiment during the month, but the improvement does not mean cost pressures have disappeared. Consumers continue to face concerns about the prices of energy, goods and services, while the labor-market outlook remains an important influence on spending decisions.

For retailers and consumer-facing companies, confidence surveys can provide an early indication of willingness to make larger purchases, travel or spend on discretionary items. However, survey sentiment is not the same as actual retail sales, and businesses should compare it with transaction data and household income trends.

The October rebound is a positive signal for the near-term outlook, but the longer-term trend and persistent affordability concerns remain important risks for the U.S. consumer economy.

Source: The Conference Board, October 27, 2026 — https://www.conference-board.org/topics/consumer-confidence/

title: U.S. Business Activity Cools Slightly as Companies Continue Raising Prices
content:
U.S. private-sector business activity slowed modestly in October, while strong demand allowed many companies to keep raising prices, according to the flash survey from S&P Global reported on October 23. The composite output index eased to 57.6 from 58.4 in September, remaining above the 50-point level that signals expansion.

The survey indicated that manufacturing strength was partly offset by a slight pullback in services. New orders edged higher, while the measure of prices charged by businesses rose to its highest level since August 2022. Supplier delivery times also deteriorated, pointing to renewed supply-chain pressure.

The combination matters for companies planning inventory, staffing and pricing. Strong orders can support revenue, but higher input costs and delivery delays can squeeze margins or force businesses to pass costs on to customers. That can complicate the inflation outlook for households and policymakers.

The survey is an early indicator rather than a final measure of economic output. Investors and business owners will compare it with official inflation, employment and spending data to assess whether demand is cooling enough to ease price pressures.

Source: Reuters reporting on S&P Global's flash PMI, October 23, 2026 — https://www.investing.com/news/economy-news/us-business-activity-cools-in-october-strong-demand-fueling-price-pressures-4969791

title: Amazon Posts $201.9 Billion in Third-Quarter Sales as AWS Growth Accelerates
content:
Amazon reported third-quarter 2026 net sales of $201.94 billion, up 12% from a year earlier, while earnings per share came in below analysts' expectations, according to the Associated Press. Amazon Web Services was a standout: cloud revenue rose 39.3% to $46 billion, its fastest growth in nearly five years.

The company said the timing of Prime Day affected the comparison between quarters. It also outlined substantial investment plans for data centers and artificial-intelligence infrastructure, while forecasting fourth-quarter sales below the midpoint of analyst expectations. Investors therefore had to weigh strong cloud momentum against spending needs and a cautious holiday-quarter outlook.

AWS growth highlights continued demand for cloud capacity and AI-related services. At the same time, large capital commitments can pressure free cash flow, especially when new infrastructure takes time to reach full utilization and generate returns.

For the wider technology sector, Amazon's results reinforce the importance of separating revenue growth from investment costs. Customers and investors will be watching cloud demand, operating margins and the pace at which AI infrastructure spending produces sustainable cash flow.

Source: Associated Press, October 30, 2026 — https://apnews.com/article/2de72b65d63006a7ce85eab441e2d6b7

title: Intel Shares Plunge as Weak PC Outlook Adds to Concerns About AI Costs
content:
Intel shares suffered a severe decline on October 30 after the chipmaker issued a weaker-than-expected outlook for the next quarter and warned that it did not expect positive cash flow for the year, Reuters reported. The forecast intensified investor concerns about the cost pressures facing parts of the semiconductor industry.

The company cited a challenging environment for PC-related demand and higher costs, including pressure associated with memory components. The news arrived as investors were already reassessing the scale of spending required to build artificial-intelligence infrastructure and the effect that spending may have on technology companies' finances.

The reaction illustrates how the AI investment cycle can create winners and pressure points across the supply chain. Demand for advanced computing can benefit some chip and data-center suppliers, while higher component costs and uneven consumer-device demand can weigh on other manufacturers.

Intel's outlook is one company's signal, not a complete measure of the semiconductor market. Buyers and investors will need to track future guidance, product execution, cash flow and demand across PCs, servers and AI accelerators.

Source: Reuters, October 30, 2026 — https://www.investing.com/news/stock-market-news/intel-warning-sparks-chip-rout-pc-weakness-clouds-turnaround-4987123

title: Microsoft Offers Voluntary Buyouts to About 60,000 Employees
content:
Microsoft has offered voluntary buyouts to approximately 60,000 employees as the company adjusts its workforce while increasing investment in artificial intelligence, according to reporting by Reuters and the Associated Press on October 26. The program covers eligible employees in participating teams across several countries, including the United States.

The offer represents a significant workforce measure for a company that reported 223,000 full-time employees globally at the end of June. Microsoft has been committing substantial capital to AI infrastructure, and the latest program highlights the organizational changes that can accompany a shift in technology priorities.

For the technology industry, the development raises questions about how companies balance investment in computing capacity, product development and staffing. AI adoption can create demand for new skills while changing the structure of some existing roles, but the effects differ across teams and business units.

A voluntary buyout offer is not the same as a confirmed reduction of the entire eligible group. The eventual number of departures and the impact on individual products or services will depend on employee participation and the company's operating plans.

Source: Reuters, October 26, 2026 — https://www.reuters.com/technology/microsoft-is-offering-buyouts-around-60000-employees-business-insider-reports-2026-10-26/

title: Alphabet Reports 25% Revenue Growth as Google Cloud Revenue Surges 103%
content:
Alphabet reported third-quarter 2026 revenue of $127.6 billion, an increase of 25% year over year, in results released on October 28. Google Cloud revenue rose 103% to $30.7 billion, reflecting demand for enterprise AI infrastructure, AI solutions and core cloud services, according to the company's filing with the U.S. Securities and Exchange Commission.

Google Services revenue increased 11% to $96.3 billion, while consolidated operating income rose 30%. Alphabet said AI investments were contributing to growth in Search queries and cloud demand. The results show how the company is monetizing several parts of its technology portfolio while expanding its infrastructure commitments.

The figures also illustrate the scale of competition in cloud computing. Businesses evaluating providers will continue to compare performance, reliability, security, pricing and the availability of specialized AI hardware, not just headline growth rates.

Strong quarterly revenue does not remove the need to assess capital expenditure and cash generation. Investors will be looking for evidence that rapid cloud expansion can translate into durable margins and returns on the resources being deployed.

Source: Alphabet, third-quarter 2026 results filed with the SEC, October 28, 2026 — https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1652044/000165204426000080/googexhibit991q32026.htm

title: Nasdaq Faces Pressure as Investors Reassess Big Tech's AI Spending Plans
content:
Technology shares came under pressure in late October as investors questioned whether the enormous cost of artificial-intelligence infrastructure will generate returns quickly enough. Reuters reported on October 30 that the Nasdaq 100 had fallen more than 5.8% during the month, putting more than $2 trillion in market value at risk.

The debate intensified after several large technology companies outlined higher spending plans for data centers, chips and related infrastructure. Investors are examining not only the pace of AI adoption but also how projects are financed, how quickly capacity is used and when new services can produce recurring revenue.

The implications extend beyond the largest technology companies. Data-center construction, networking equipment, power suppliers and semiconductor manufacturers are all connected to the investment cycle, although their exposure and ability to capture profits vary.

A falling index does not prove that AI demand is disappearing. It indicates that market participants are reassessing valuations, financing requirements and expected returns. Cash flow, cloud growth and capital-expenditure guidance will remain important measures in upcoming reports.

Source: Reuters, October 30, 2026 — https://www.reuters.com/business/media-telecom/nasdaq-faces-2-trillion-wipeout-october-ai-spending-fears-deepen-2026-10-30/

title: Wall Street Suffers Sharp Sell-Off as Intel and Amazon Deepen AI Spending Worries
content:
U.S. stocks fell sharply on Friday, October 30, as disappointing corporate outlooks and concerns about the cost of artificial-intelligence investment weighed on technology shares. Reuters reported that the Nasdaq Composite dropped 2.9% and the S&P 500 fell 1.8% during the session.

The declines followed fresh scrutiny of spending plans and cash generation at major technology companies. Intel's weak outlook added pressure to semiconductor shares, while Amazon's large infrastructure commitments and cautious sales forecast reinforced questions about the returns from the AI buildout.

Market moves were not uniform across sectors. Investors continued to evaluate earnings, energy prices, interest-rate expectations and the relative resilience of businesses outside the largest technology names. A sharp decline in a market-weighted index can also reflect outsized moves in a small group of very large companies.

The session underscores why investors should look beyond daily index changes. Company guidance, cash flow, debt levels and demand trends can help distinguish a broad economic deterioration from a repricing of a particular investment theme.

Source: Reuters, October 30, 2026 — https://www.reuters.com/business/nasdaq-futures-tumble-amazon-intel-results-deepen-ai-spending-woes-2026-10-30/

title: Belden Reports Record Third-Quarter Revenue and $100 Million Data Center Agreement
content:
Networking solutions company Belden reported record third-quarter 2026 revenue of $966 million, up 38% from a year earlier, and adjusted earnings per share of $2.26, up 15%. The company also announced an agreement to supply $100 million in fiber solutions to a major U.S. data-center customer in 2027.

Belden said quarterly orders reached $1.017 billion, rising 46% year over year, while demand for networking infrastructure was supported by data-center investment and automation. The company noted that its data-center business is expected to grow by more than 50% next year, based on current plans and market conditions.

The announcement offers a view into the suppliers that support the expansion of AI and cloud infrastructure. Data centers require extensive fiber connectivity and networking equipment, creating opportunities for companies beyond chip designers and cloud operators.

Investors should distinguish adjusted measures from GAAP results and consider integration costs, supply-chain conditions and the timing of customer projects. The announced agreement is a company-specific development, but it reflects the broader demand for physical infrastructure behind digital services.

Source: Belden press release published by Nasdaq, October 29, 2026 — https://www.nasdaq.com/press-release/belden-reports-record-third-quarter-2026-results-and-announces-100-million-data
